saints.name: St. Ethelbert of Kent
saints.title: King
saints.shortBlurb: The first Christian king among the English, who welcomed St. Augustine of Canterbury and gave the Gospel a home in his realm…
biography: Ethelbert, king of Kent from about 589, was reckoned by Bede the third English king to hold overlordship south of the Humber. He had married Bertha, the Christian daughter of the Frankish king Charibert, who worshipped at St. Martin's in Canterbury with her chaplain Bishop Liudhard.

When Augustine landed on the Isle of Thanet in 597 with some forty monks sent by Pope St. Gregory the Great, Ethelbert met them in the open air for fear of enchantment, then gave them a dwelling in Canterbury and leave to preach. He was himself baptized soon after, by tradition on 1 June 597, the first Christian king of the English.

By his favour Canterbury became England's mother church; he helped convert his nephew Saeberht of Essex and founded the first church of St. Paul in London and of St. Andrew at Rochester. His code of laws in ninety sections is the earliest written law in any Germanic tongue.

He died on 24 February 616 and was buried beside Bertha in the abbey church of Saints Peter and Paul at Canterbury, where he was long venerated as a saint; the Roman Martyrology honours him as the first English king to be converted to Christ.
saints.knownFor: Receiving St. Augustine of Canterbury and becoming the first Christian English king.

sources.text: Bede, Ecclesiastical History of the English People (public-domain translation)
